confirmed.title: Unfunded fresh accounts get free, self-perpetuating block space: fail-open balance gate + zero-cost executor refusal + infinite mempool requeue
confirmed.claim: The onboarding design makes an account with no CoinStore pass the mempool balance gate (fail-open), the executor refuses its transaction WITHOUT charging anything or consuming a nonce (deduct_gas prologue aborts -> `return None`), and the mempool's inflight loan ledger then re-queues that same transaction every 30s forever because it never appears in `executed_raws`. confirmed.title: Pre-staged CoinStore write survives user-payload abort: anyone can force-create CoinStore<T> for ANY type T at ANY address without holding T
confirmed.claim: `auto_register_writes` trusts `call.ty_args.first()` verbatim and stages `resource_{recipient}_0x1::coin::CoinStore<T>` = 0 before execution; the staged map is returned even when the user stage aborts (vm_move lib.rs:608/617). So a sender who owns no CoinStore<T> at all (withdraw aborts immediately) still lands a third-party state write at the recipient for an attacker-chosen T, including types from attacker-published modules or type tags that do not resolve at all. This is a third-party-controlled state mutation the doc comment claims cannot happen ("It grants nothing"), with concrete downstream effects: it flips a validator's epoch reward disposition in staking.move:478 from compound-into-stake to liquid payout, makes `coin::register<T>`/`wbtc::register` permanently abort for the victim for that T, and allows unbounded resource-key bloat under arbitrary struct tags at any address.

confirmed.title: auto_register_writes treats a RocksDB read error as 'store absent' and will overwrite an existing balance with zero
confirmed.claim: The existence check is `matches!(self.db.get(&key), Ok(Some(_)))`, so `Err(_)` from RocksDB falls through to staging a zero CoinStore. Because the prestaged write is committed in the same WriteBatch (and is only overridden by a later user-stage write if the transfer succeeds), a transient read error on one node during a transfer to a funded recipient zeroes that recipient's balance on that node only, destroying funds and forking its state root from the rest of the network. The code comment asserts this path 'never overwrite[s] a balance'; the surrounding executor treats DB write errors as fatal (panic at lib.rs ~1700) but this read is fail-open.

A transfer S->R of 10 AIN executes on node N while RocksDB returns an I/O error for that single `get` (disk hiccup, corrupted SST, fd exhaustion). 3. auto_register_writes stages `(key_R, Some(bcs(0u128)))`. 4a. If the user stage also fails to read R (same error surfaced through `OverlayStorage` -> `AINCOREStorage::get_resource`), the payload aborts and the zero-store prestaged write is still committed (vm_move lib.rs:617) — R's balance on node N becomes 0 while other nodes keep 1,000,000 -> state root divergence at this height. 4b. If the overlay read succeeds, `staged` now says R has 0, the Move deposit reads the overlay first (overlay.rs:89-92) and computes 0+10=10, and the user write commits 10 — R lost 999,990 on node N. Either way the node forks; no panic, no log beyond the auto-register print.

confirmed.claim: A transaction that can never execute (future nonce, already-consumed nonce, or an unfunded fresh sender) is admitted by the mempool, pulled into a vertex, rejected by the executor with `return None` (so it is NOT in `executed_raws`), stays in `inflight`, and is returned to `pending_txs` by `requeue_stale` every 30s forever.
